django_octo is the modular core orchestrator for the Django-Octo framework ecosystem. It unifies decoupled runtime modules under a single installation entrypoint, providing automated environment discovery, live Dual-Channel observability, and event-driven cumulative versioning.

Designed to remain completely agnostic to domain logic, this core hub dynamically detects active satellite modules installed in the runtime environment (importlib.util.find_spec + importlib.metadata) and mounts their administrative and public surfaces without manual wiring or tight coupling.

docs.title: Key Architectural Features
docs.text:
• Zero-Config Environment Auto-Discovery: Exposes get_installed_octo_apps() and dynamic URL mounting (include("django_octo.urls")), automatically registering only the satellite modules present in the active virtual environment.
  • Automated Control Hub (/octo/): Built-in zero-dependency observability dashboard that introspects installed modules, displays live semantic versions, and bridges direct access between public channels and the Django Admin panel.
  • Event-Driven Cumulative Versioning: Driven by repository_dispatch webhooks from satellite CI/CD pipelines. Every release published in a satellite module automatically increments the core version queue, updates CHANGELOG.md, validates cross-module coupling tests, and publishes a verified release to PyPI via OIDC Trusted Publishing.
  • Rye Environment Integration: Fully integrated with the Rust-based Python package manager for deterministic dependency locking across the entire ecosystem.

docs.title: Installation & Quick Start (PyPI)
docs.text: Install the entire unified ecosystem into any modern Django (>=6.1.2) and Python (>=3.12) project using pip or Rye:

docs.title: 1. Install Core Package
docs.text:
pip install django-octo
Or using the Rust-backed Rye package manager: 
rye add django-octo

docs.title: 2. Auto-Register Apps & Migrate
docs.text:
Use get_installed_octo_apps() in your settings.py to automatically load the orchestrator alongside every detected satellite module: 

from django_octo import get_installed_octo_apps

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    "django.contrib.admin",
    "django.contrib.auth",
    "django.contrib.contenttypes",
    "django.contrib.sessions",
    "django.contrib.messages",
    "django.contrib.staticfiles",
    *get_installed_octo_apps(),
]
Apply all unified database migrations in a single pass: 
python3 manage.py migrate

docs.title: 3. Mount the Unified Router
docs.text:
Include django_octo.urls in your root urls.py to expose the Control Hub and all active module endpoints simultaneously: 

from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import include, path

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),
    path("", include("django_octo.urls")),
]
Start the server (python3 manage.py runserver) and navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8000/ to inspect the live Control Hub.

docs.title: Local Sandbox & Development Setup (Using Rye)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jeanpmodev/django_octo/
cd django_octo
rye sync
rye test

docs.title: django-octo-aurora pypi library package
docs.text:
django_octo_aurora is a decoupled runtime software topology visualizer and interactive architecture showcase module under the Django-Octo ecosystem.

It inspects the host Django project structure, installed apps, AST metrics, and local Git commit history in real time, persisting lightweight snapshots for single-query rendering across both a public showcase endpoint and the Django Admin interface.

docs.title: Core Architecture
docs.text:
• Dual-Channel Access: Exposes an interactive HTML5 Canvas topology view on a dedicated route (/aurora/) and embeds the same preview directly inside the Django Admin (Aurora Snapshots).
  • Runtime Introspection: Scans active project directories (pathlib), extracts Python class/function counts (ast), detects coupled INSTALLED_APPS, and parses local Git history (git log) using only the Python standard library.
  • Single-Query Persistence: Stores serialized topology payloads in AuroraSnapshot, ensuring subsequent page loads execute in a single ORM query.
  • Interactive Canvas Controls: Supports directional navigation (keyboard arrows / WASD and on-screen D-Pad), module filtering checklists, file-type counters, commit timeline playback, presentation mode (H), and clean PNG export.

docs.title: 1. Install Package
docs.text:
pip install django-octo-aurora
Or using Rye: 
rye add django-octo-aurora

docs.title: 2. Register App & Migrate
docs.text:
Add "django_octo_aurora" to INSTALLED_APPS in settings.py: 

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ...
    "django_octo_aurora",
]
Run migrations: 
python3 manage.py migrate

docs.title: 3. Mount Routes
docs.text:
Include the module URLs in your project's urls.py: 

from django.contrib import admin
from django.urls import include, path

urlpatterns = [
    path("admin/", admin.site.urls),
    path("aurora/", include("django_octo_aurora.urls")),
]
Start the server (python3 manage.py runserver) and open http://127.0.0.1:8000 or http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin/django_octo_aurora/aurorasnapshot/.

docs.title: Local Development (Rye)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jeanpmodev/django_octo_aurora.git
cd django_octo_aurora
rye sync
rye run pytest
rye run behave

See TESTING.md for full QA and load testing instructions.

docs.title: Django-Octo UML
docs.text:
Interactive runtime Django entity-relationship and UML architecture visualizer under the Django-Octo ecosystem.

django-octo-uml inspects your active Django models at runtime, renders interactive SVG diagrams inside Django Admin, and archives timestamped snapshots so you can track your data model evolution over time.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python >= 3.12
  • Django >= 6.0
  • System Graphviz (dot binary) for SVG/PNG rendering (sudo apt install graphviz or brew install graphviz)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install django-octo-uml

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Add django_octo_uml to INSTALLED_APPS in settings.py:
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ...
    "django.contrib.admin",
    "django_octo_uml",
]
  1. Run migrations to create the snapshot history table:
python manage.py migrate django_octo_uml
  1. Open Admin -> UML -> UML Architecture to generate snapshots, browse architecture history, and export .dot, .svg, or .png files.
